author: Adam Uren
title: Deadly Minneapolis mass shooting: Wounded officers expected to survive - NewsBreak
text:
By Adam Uren ,
5 hours ago A mass shooting at a downtown Minneapolis apartment complex left three people dead, including the suspect, and multiple people injured – including three police officers – on Wednesday.
The shooting unfolded at 15 E. Grant St. just after 4:30 p.m. at the Shoreline Plaza apartment complex, formerly known as the Loring Towers. Residents are displaced Wednesday night as the investigation unfolds and at least six people are hospitalized.
“I can’t emphasize enough how dangerous this situation was and how heroic our officers were in their response,” Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey said, confirming one officer was shot in the leg and another officer sustained two gunshot wounds to the abdomen.
Interim Chief of Police Bill Peterson had no comment on a potential motive at a press conference Wednesday night, but he confirmed officers were familiar with the suspect.
Bring Me The News
Peterson also told reporters he had no information regarding the ages of those shot, nor knowledge of their relationship to the property or the suspect.
The two officers wounded in the shooting and a third officer injured during the incident are all expected to recover, according to Peterson.
The city said four additional officers experienced adverse effects after being exposed to an unknown airborne substance and two other officers were hurt in a car crash while responding to the scene.
Peterson said he’s sickened and saddened by the incident, which he described as “senseless.”
Officers enountered gunfire, haze inside apartment complex Police initially responded to reports of gunfire and information that one person had been shot just after 4:30 p.m., according to the city.
Inside the apartment building, police discovered shooting victims and followed the sound of gunfire to an upper floor where they “encountered a haze that significantly limited their visibility.”
One victim and the suspect died at the scene and the third victim died at Hennepin County Medical Center, the city confirmed.
At Wednesday night’s press conference, Peterson said it was too early to say what caused the haze inside the apartment complex.
Court filings reveal eviction proceedings Details emerging from early court filings suggest that the suspected shooter had been facing eviction over gun flashing and statements he’d made that he would “kill someone”.
The suspect had also been accused of assaulting another resident on the property in March, according to FOX 9.
While details about a potential motive remain scare, early details suggest the shooting may bear some resemblance to a triple killing at a St. Paul apartment leasing office earlier this summer. In that case, a 31-year-old man is accused of executing three employees after being told he could not cancel his parking garage contract .
On Wednesday evening, Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty said: “While we still have limited information, it is clear that this was a terrible and shocking attack with numerous victims.
“Our hearts go out to the families and loved ones of the deceased, the law enforcement officers who were shot, and all the other victims who are currently receiving medical care.
“We are currently working with MPD and the BCA to gather information. Anyone who has information regarding this attack should contact law enforcement or our office.”
summary: Interim Chief of Police Bill Peterson had no comment on a potential motive at a press conference Wednesday night, but he confirmed officers were familiar with the suspect. Peterson also told reporters he had no information regarding the ages of those shot, nor knowledge of their relationship to the property or the suspect. At Wednesday night’s press conference, Peterson said it was too early to say what caused the haze inside the apartment complex.
